claim: Wald worked on estimating how likely aircraft were to survive hits in different places
source_url: https://www.cna.org/analyses/1980/a-method-of-estimating-plane-vulnerability (CRC 432, July 1980, reprint of Wald's SRG memoranda; full text read via lru.praxis.dk copy) + abstract of https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1984.10478038 (OpenAlex)

claim: The data came from planes that returned; Wald's methods took into account that planes hit in the most dangerous places were less likely to return
source_url: https://www.cna.org/analyses/1980/a-method-of-estimating-plane-vulnerability (CRC 432, July 1980, reprint of Wald's SRG memoranda; full text read via lru.praxis.dk copy) + abstract of https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1984.10478038 (OpenAlex)

Caveat for a note: Wald assumes the distribution of hits over areas is known (his numerical example takes it proportional to area) and his worked examples are hypothetical.
